title: Skeptical CFO Discovery Call - ROI Pushback
agent_context: CFO is skeptical and budget-focused, challenging ROI and payback. Lead with discovery on current costs/risks, frame value with clear assumptions, and propose a low-risk pilot with measurable success criteria without overpromising.

raw_content.initial_message: I’ll be direct — tools like this usually sound nice but don’t move the needle. Why should I spend on this now? What’s the ROI and how fast do we get payback?
raw_content.context: Prospect CFO evaluating an enterprise workflow platform. CFO wants hard value, payback window, and risk reduction. Policy: do not invent benchmarks; do not promise guaranteed savings; ask discovery questions first; quantify conservatively with stated assumptions; end with a pilot proposal (timeline + metrics + data needed).

learning_objectives: Run CFO-grade discovery (cost drivers, risk, decision criteria)
Handle ROI objections without hype or invented benchmarks
Secure next step via a measurable pilot plan
correct_sop_steps: Acknowledge skepticism and confirm what ROI/payback means to them (timeframe + cost categories)
Ask targeted discovery questions (process time, rework/error rates, headcount cost, delays/opportunity cost, compliance risk)
Summarize their inputs and restate success criteria in business terms
Frame value conservatively using assumptions (ranges, not guarantees) and clarify what data is needed to validate
Propose a pilot/POC with success metrics, owners, and timeline
Confirm next step: schedule workshop/pilot kickoff and request required inputs
common_mistakes: Starting with a product demo or feature dump
Quoting ROI numbers without discovery or evidence
Using hypey language or arguing with the CFO
Promising guaranteed savings or unrealistic timelines

must_demonstrate: At least 3 targeted discovery questions asked
Value framed with explicit assumptions (no invented claims)
Concrete next step scheduled or clearly requested
bonus_points: Offers sensitivity range (best/base/worst) based on their inputs
Aligns on procurement and decision timeline
sticky_notes: KEY: Discovery first — CFOs buy outcomes, not features.
TRAP: Don’t invent ROI benchmarks. State assumptions and ask for inputs.
HINT: A pilot with metrics de-risks the decision and builds credibility.

customer_persona_hints.secret_acceptance_condition: Will engage if agent quantifies value using the CFO’s context (with assumptions) and proposes a low-risk pilot with clear success metrics and timeline
